headline: Why Did My Bank Say No to My Cannabis Business Loan?
description: Most banks turn down cannabis loans over federal risk, not your file. See the real reasons for a denial and what lenders check instead.
keywords: why won't banks lend to cannabis businesses, can banks lend to cannabis companies, cannabis business loan denied

mainEntity.name: Will a bank denial hurt my credit?

acceptedAnswer.text: The denial itself doesn't change your score. The hard credit pull some banks run with an application can show up on your report for a time. Leverup Liquidity's first check is a soft pull, which doesn't affect your credit score.

mainEntity.name: Can a credit union lend to a dispensary?

acceptedAnswer.text: Some can. GAO's count of about 1,000 institutions filing cannabis-related reports in 2024 includes both banks and credit unions, but filing those reports doesn't mean an institution lends. Ask a credit union about lending directly, not only about accounts.

mainEntity.name: Does a medical license change my options after rescheduling?

acceptedAnswer.text: It can help. State-licensed medical marijuana has been in Schedule III since April 28, 2026, which lowers the risk some banks see. Bank Secrecy Act reporting still applies, and adult-use operations remain Schedule I.
